title: Asking Questions That Actually Work
brief: Rewrite 8 poorly worded questions from Meridian colleagues. Run each against the
Wealth agent and paste in the SQL it produced.
You are marked on the rewrites, not the SQL.
Two of the eight cannot be fixed by rewording at all — the data cannot answer them,
or the question hides a definition nobody has settled. Say which two, and why.
Recognising a question Genie should not be asked is the skill being tested.

checks.name: Prerequisite: an agent exists to ask
checks.hint: Run notebook 08_agents, or build your own in the Genie UI.

review: Each rewrite names a period, a currency and a definition where the original left them open.
Exactly two are identified as unanswerable, and they are the right two.
The reason given is about the data or the definition, not about phrasing.
The pasted SQL is read, not just pasted — the learner says whether it did what they meant.

inputs.title: The eight questions, exactly as colleagues wrote them
rows: 8. "How many clients do we have and are they growing"
Rewrite each so a stranger would produce the same number you meant. Name the
period, the currency, and which definition you want.
Two of the eight cannot be fixed by rewording. Find them, and say why — the
reason must be about the data or an unsettled definition, not the phrasing.
